keyFindings.description: A /new during the start claim: claimWith registered the old session (sessionID read at :190, recorded at :250) but sends the start message into the new session, whose legion calls are refused (isClaimedSession false) until the switch's queued re-claim registers it; the role claim for the old session then fails and the warning (:357) says 'The start turn has the controller's registration; run /legion-claim-controller', both false (the queued re-claim does it; following the instruction rotates the secret once more). legion.test.ts:3161 pins that notice. Fix: after the registration, when the current session is not the registered one, do not send (startMessageSent stays false) and let the queued re-claim send it in the new session; word the warning for that case.
Previous finding 6 open on one path: startCommand calls serialised directly, so a second /legion-controller-start behind a hung claim waits with no notice; the docs say every waiting claim says so.

The re-claim warning says the session keeps its registration whenever controllerSessionID equals the current session, including when the re-claim failed before registering (state() error, 403 because a later `legion controller start` revoked the capability), so it can say set_status still works when every grant fails. Decide from whether this claim registered.
The row 'the claim that sent it, or a later one, did not finish' does not match claimComplete, which resets only once a registration is in (:247).
